stone_tuchman_review.title: Lawrence Stone, “The Worst of Times?” New York Review of Books, 28 September 1978.
stone_tuchman_review.citation: Lawrence Stone, “The Worst of Times?” New York Review of Books, 28 September 1978.

verification.note: Complete review of A Distant Mirror read. Stone praises scholarship and narrative communication while criticizing analogy, biographical focus and selection of events over institutional/economic explanation. His uses of Geertz and Veblen are his interventions, not those authors’ direct reviews. His own progress and historical claims remain attributed. This is distinct from his 1979 Past & Present article, whose full text remains unread.

fox_stone_tuchman_exchange.title: Elizabeth Fox-Genovese and Lawrence Stone, “Tuchman and History,” New York Review of Books, 7 December 1978.
fox_stone_tuchman_exchange.citation: Elizabeth Fox-Genovese and Lawrence Stone, “Tuchman and History,” New York Review of Books, 7 December 1978.

verification.note: Complete letter and Stone reply read. Fox-Genovese challenges professional prestige as a criterion and Stone’s crisis/progress assumptions, defending narrative’s treatment of groups and material dislocation while explicitly distinguishing Tuchman from Marxism. Stone defends differences between synthesis and innovative research and qualifies his progress claim. Tuchman is the subject, not an author of this exchange; neither reviewer’s historical claims are independently verified here.

w3_guha_chibber_verso_2014.title: Vivek Chibber, response to Partha Chatterjee ("Subaltern Studies Revisited"), with an introduction by Clément Petitjean, Verso, 25 February 2014.
w3_guha_chibber_verso_2014.citation: Vivek Chibber, response to Partha Chatterjee ("Subaltern Studies Revisited"), with an introduction by Clément Petitjean, Verso, 25 February 2014.

verification.note: Read in part for revision 1.151: the introduction and the sections "Guha and the Bourgeois Revolutions" and "Does Guha refer to the bourgeois revolutions?". Petitjean: "In April 2013, at the annual Historical Materialism conference held in New York, Vivek Chibber appeared alongside Partha Chatterjee in a much-anticipated critical debate." Chibber: "I argue in PTSC that Guha's work is both foundational for the entire Subalternist project ... and that it is fundamentally flawed. Its flaw is that it generates a set of contrastive claims about the Indian bourgeoisie and Indian capitalism that rest on a comparison with the European achievement. But the comparison fails because Guha quite dramatically misunderstands the European story"; "the European bourgeoisie was no more committed to an integrated political culture than was its Indian counterpart". Chatterjee's three replies, as Chibber reports them (Chatterjee's text is unread): Guha makes no claims about the classic bourgeois revolutions, only about the historiography of colonial India; "Indian bourgeoisie" means the Congress's middle-class leadership; any European referent is the mid-twentieth-century British state. Chibber quotes Dominance without Hegemony p. 19 (the bourgeoisie's "historic triumphs in England in 1648 and France in 1789") and p. 5 (its "failure to measure up to the heroism of the European bourgeoisie in its period of ascendancy").
